incident-bot: ALERT: streaming-route p99 latency spike detected (>3.2s) for model=gptx-8k in us-west-2 — SLO breach started at 2026-03-14T21:11:16Z. autoscale: no errors. kv-cache eviction-rate up 4x, prefill_dequeue > decode_queue by 45%. paging events increasing, some worker OOMs reported. link: https://console.redwood/alerts/3551239876 :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): I'm looking. p95 jumped to 1.1s, p99 3.4s on streaming endpoints. Streaming stalls and tail latency. Starting triage. @eng-runtime-alert can you dump recent eviction metrics and active prefill queue sizes?

eng-runtime-alert: Metrics snapshot attached: kv_eviction_rate: 402/s -> baseline 95/s, kv_frag_ratio: 0.62, prefill_queue_len: 312, decode_queue_len: 215, paging_io_wait: 120ms -> baseline 30ms. Top shards: shard-12, shard-7.

josh: Noted. Any spike in cold-decode failures? could be prefill vs decode imbalance causing decode tasks to pile up and trigger paging.

samir: Logs show repeated prefill task retries on shard-12, errors: "KVPrefillTimeout" then large decode batches arrive after prefill finally completes. Looks like prefill workers are slower than decoders for some shards (disk-backed prefill).

maria (oncall): So hypothesis: high eviction -> fragmentation causes prefill reader thrash -> decode starvation and tail stalls. Customer impact: CS bot reports a handful of enterprise customers with elevated token latency and streaming stalls; no 5xxs yet, but degraded UX. @customer-success-bot please list top impacted orgs.

customer-success-bot: Impacted customers (automated): "Shopora", "Travelly", "OpsLens" — increased streaming latency and multiple timed-out completions. Severity flagged to account owners.

josh: Quick mitigations we can try in parallel:
- increase kv cache soft limit for busy shards to reduce eviction pressure
- temporarily disable aggressive prefill for streaming-route (fall back to on-demand decode)
- reroute heavy customers to a dedicated capacity pool (if available)
- throttle large-batch decodes to smooth consumption

maria (oncall): Agree. I'll incrementally apply: 1) bump kv_cache_threshold from 0.72 -> 0.85 for shard-12 and shard-7, 2) set prefill_rate_limit to 0.6 for streaming-route, 3) create a temporary traffic-split to dedicated-pool-2 at 10% for top 3 orgs. Applying now.

eng-runtime-alert: Command executed: 
```
# increase soft limit for two shards
rdw admin kv set-soft-limit --shard shard-12 --value 0.85
rdw admin kv set-soft-limit --shard shard-7 --value 0.85
# throttle prefill for streaming-route
rdw routes update streaming-route --prefill-rate 0.6
# create split
rdw traffic split create --route streaming-route --target dedicated-pool-2 --percent 10 --reason "latency mitigation"
```
Applied with minor propagation delay.

kai: Any immediate improvement on p99? watching dashboards.

eng-runtime-alert: After changes (t+90s): kv_eviction_rate -> 110/s, prefill_queue_len -> 78, decode_queue_len -> 95, paging_io_wait -> 38ms. p95 -> 420ms, p99 -> 1.05s. Streaming stalls reduced by ~65%.

maria (oncall): Good signal. Continue monitoring for 20m. We'll keep the traffic split and rate limit until stable. Need to follow up with a root cause: why prefill workers fell behind (IO, thread starvation, or config drift).

samir: I see prefill worker nodes on shard-12 had degraded disk performance (iostat shows high latency) due to background snapshot job that started around the same time. Snapshots were scheduled by infra job infra-snap-2 at 21:05Z. Snap jobs coincided with eviction spike.

josh: If snapshot is root cause, we need to adjust snapshot timing and/or ensure prefill uses hot cache SSDs. For immediate safety: blacklist snapshot on nodes serving critical shards during peak windows. I'll open infra ticket.

maria (oncall): Noted. Escalating to infra: @infra-team can you confirm and throttle the snapshot jobs on nodes with high prefill load?

eng-runtime-alert: infra-team acknowledged. Snapshot paused on affected nodes.

josh: Also pushing a short-term config change to make prefill backoff more aggressive on transient IO errors to avoid retry storms. Patch in staging looks safe. Rolling to prod canary to 5% now.

maria (oncall): Canary result: reduced retries and smoother queueing. Patch looks good. Rolling to 50% and monitoring.

eng-runtime-alert: Observed stable metrics t+12m after start: p95 380ms, p99 720ms, eviction_rate ~90/s, prefill_queue_len ~32. No additional paging spikes.

maria (oncall): Customer impact update: CS bot reports most impacted orgs recovered; Shopora saw repeated streams restored. Logging follow-up notes to incident doc. Creating post-incident follow-up items: (1) investigate snapshot scheduling + IO isolation, (2) revisit prefill vs decode worker sizing, (3) add alert for prefill_queue_len to warn before paging.

samir: I'll take item 2 and 3. josh take 1 with infra.

maria (oncall): Handoff: my shift ends in 20m. @kai please take incident lead for ongoing monitoring and postmortem coordination. Key artifacts: mitigation actions above, metrics snapshots, snapshot job id infra-snap-2, and canary rollout ID rdw-roll-4873.

kai: Taking handoff. I'll keep the traffic split at 10% for 30m and rollback if metrics regress. Setting a reminder for postmortem doc and linking owners.

maria (oncall): Thanks team. Closing active mitigation updates; will follow up in postmortem. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: SLOs back within thresholds at 2026-03-14T21:40:20Z. Duration: ~29m. Incident severity: SEV3 (customer impact but no 5xxs). Postmortem link: https://confluence.redwood/incident/3551239876-postmortem
